answer_summary: Overall balanced BZ reaction: 3 CH2(COOH)2 (malonic acid) + 4 BrO3- -> 9 CO2 + 4 Br- + 6 H2O. Atoms conserved (C 9=9, H 12=12, O 24=24, Br 4=4) and charge conserved (-4=-4). Derived by the half-reaction method from the problem-stated notes: MA -> CO2 releases 8 e- per MA, BrO3- -> Br- consumes 6 e- per bromate, lcm(8,6)=24 gives the 3:4 stoichiometry; Ce(IV) is a catalyst and cancels out, K+ and sulfate are spectators.
assumptions: All species and redox directions are taken from the problem statement and its note (MA oxidised to CO2, BrO3- reduced to Br-, Ce(IV) catalyst, acidic H2SO4 medium).

Standard oxidation-number conventions H=+1, O=-2 (fractional averages allowed) used only to derive the electron ledger; the final equation is certified by atom and charge balance, which is premise-free.
K+ and SO4(2-) treated as spectator ions of the stated reactant salts/medium; they appear on neither side of the overall equation.
